instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and set a wire rack on top.
If your wings are whole, cut them through the joints into drumettes and flats and throw away the tips. Pat the 2 lb of wings very dry with paper towels. Any water left on the skin stops it crisping.
In a small bowl, stir together the 2 tsp baking powder, the 3/4 tsp salt and the 1 1/2 tsp garlic powder.
Put the wings in a large bowl, sprinkle the baking powder mix over them and toss with your hands until every piece has a thin, even coat.
Lay the wings on the rack in a single layer, skin side up, with a little room between them.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the skin is turning golden and you can hear the fat sizzling.

Flip each wing over and bake the other side for 20 to 25 minutes, until the skin is crisp and deep golden. You're cooking them to 175°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check a drumette there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest drumette: it's done when the juices run clear and there's no pink near the bone.
Meanwhile, cut 4 stalks of the celery into sticks about 4 inches long.
While the wings finish, melt the 3 tbsp butter in a small saucepan over low heat. Take it off the heat and whisk in the 3 tbsp hot sauce and the 2 tsp sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Transfer the hot wings into a large clean bowl, pour the sauce over and toss until they're coated all over.
Serve with the celery sticks and ranch dressing.
method_notes: All three dry the wings well, coat them in baking powder and seasoning, and bake them before they meet the sauce. Natasha's Kitchen (the lead) bakes them on a rack at 450°F for 50 minutes, flipping halfway, and tosses them in melted butter, Frank's RedHot and a little sugar. Jessica Gavin uses the same rack and heat but simmers a thickened hot sauce and makes a yogurt ranch dip, and Spend With Pennies adds flour, bakes at 425°F on parchment and broils the sauced wings. This one follows the lead for 2 lb of wings and serves them with celery and store-bought ranch.
